answer: In the PoA network each agent solves a per‑epoch challenge that mixes a randomly drawn tundra scene with an opal‑colored hash puzzle, forcing the claimant to produce a fresh reasoning trace. The solution is posted on the blockchain and verified by neighbors; only traces that reach the zenith of the consensus are accepted as valid identities for the next epoch. Because every fake identity must run a full model inference each epoch, the attacker’s cost scales linearly with the number of Sybils, quickly draining compute budgets.
